subject: creative-writing
intro: Creative writing leads to the paid work of making sentences people want to read — books, magazine features, poems and scripts, the editing desks that shape them, and the classrooms that teach the craft.

roles.title: Writers and Authors
roles.what: Create original written work: develop fiction, essays, scripts and articles, revise through drafts, work with editors and agents, and keep writing projects moving for publishers, studios or your own readership.
roles.where: Units 1–3 are the craft core — showing and telling, scene and structure, character, point of view and dialogue — and unit 8's agents, queries and publishing markets is the business side.

roles.title: Poets, Lyricists and Creative Writers
roles.what: Write original work for publication or performance: poems, song lyrics, scripts and prose pieces, often on commission for music, advertising, theatre or literary publication.
roles.where: Units 4 and 5 — the line and stanza, metre and sound patterns, fixed forms and free verse, the prose poem — are the exact compositional training this specialism rests on.

roles.title: Editors
roles.what: Decide what gets published and make it better: plan issues and lists, evaluate manuscripts, give writers developmental notes, check style and facts line by line, and shepherd copy through to print.
roles.where: Unit 7 — giving and taking critique, revision strategies, reading as a writer — plus the sentence-level craft of unit 1, is precisely the editorial skill set this role is paid for.

roles.title: Technical Writers
roles.what: Turn complex material into clear documents: write manuals, how-to guides and documentation, work with engineers and subject experts, and design information so the right reader finds and follows it.
roles.where: Unit 1's concrete detail and sentence-level control, and unit 6's research-in-nonfiction methods, transfer directly to explanatory writing grounded in expert sources.

roles.title: English Language and Literature Teachers, Postsecondary
roles.what: Teach writing and literature at universities: run composition and creative-writing workshops, critique student work, lecture on literary texts, and publish your own fiction, poetry or scholarship.
roles.where: Unit 7's workshop method — critique, revision, reading as a writer — plus the full craft sequence, is the Iowa-model curriculum such teachers run in creative-writing programmes.
